cards.design_implication: When modeling thermal transport in similar insulating quantum magnets, consider separating the phonon thermal conductivity from magnetic scattering terms, assuming the field primarily affects the density of scattering centers rather than their scattering efficiency.
does_not_establish: The mechanism for systems with coherent spin transport contributions.
Microscopic details of the spin-phonon coupling beyond the phenomenological description.
Generalizability to all magnetic insulators without further verification.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Away from the magnetically ordered phase at low temperatures and small fields, there is no coherent spin contribution to the thermal conductivity, and hence the efect must be caused by a strong suppression of the phonon thermal conductivity due to magnetic fluctations, which are in turn suppressed by the field.
limitations: This mechanism is established for CrCl3 under specific conditions (away from magnetically ordered phase).
Applies to insulating quantum magnets where phonon transport dominates.
cards.statement: In CrCl3, the giant field-induced enhancement of thermal conductivity is attributed to the suppression of phonon scattering by magnetic fluctuations, rather than a coherent spin contribution to heat transport.

cards.design_implication: For high-field thermal conductivity measurements, ensure thermometry is calibrated under the maximum applied field conditions to account for magnetoresistance or field-induced temperature shifts.
does_not_establish: Calibration requirements for other types of thermometers.
Optimal temperature difference limits for non-steady-state measurements.
General experimental setup for all thermal conductivity measurements.
cards.evidence_excerpt: The in-plane longitudinal thermal conductivity, $\kappa _ { x x } \equiv \kappa ,$ was measured on an as-grown sample of dimensions $2 \times 4 \times 0 . 5$ mm using a single-heater, two-thermometer configuration in steady-state operation with the field applied in the ab plane and in the direction of the thermal gradient $( \nabla T \ \| \ \mathbf { H } \in a b )$ ; limited κ measurements were also performed with the field normal to the plane. The diference in absolute temperatures across the sample was set never to exceed 5% of the bath temperature throughout the entire T range of the measurements. All thermometry was performed using Cernox resistors, which were pre-calibrated individually and <sup>in</sup> <sup>situ</sup> under the maximum applied fields of each instrument.
limitations: Specific to the sample dimensions and configuration described.
Calibration applies to the specific instruments and fields used in this study.
cards.statement: In-plane longitudinal thermal conductivity measurements were performed using a single-heater, two-thermometer configuration with Cernox resistors pre-calibrated individually and in situ under maximum applied fields.

cards.design_implication: When analyzing thermal conductivity in magnetic insulators with strong spin-phonon coupling, consider using an empirical model that decouples the population of magnetic fluctuations from their scattering efficiency if microscopic details are unknown.
does_not_establish: Applicability to systems with field-dependent scattering efficiency.
Accuracy in regimes with coherent 3D magnon transport.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We build an empirical model for the thermal conductivity of CrCl<sub>3</sub> within a formalism assuming an independently determined number of spin-flip processes and an eficiency of the phonon scattering events they mediate. By extracting the intrinsic phonon thermal conductivity we obtain a quantitative description of our measured data at all fields and temperatures, and we demonstrate that the scattering eficiency is entirely independent of the applied field.
limitations: The model is empirical and phenomenological.
Specifically validated for CrCl3; generalizability to other systems requires testing.
cards.statement: The study employed an empirical model for thermal conductivity that assumes an independently determined number of spin-flip processes and a field-independent efficiency of phonon scattering events to describe data across various fields and temperatures.
